subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope should count as sufficient for this native-Linux VPS reasoning-latency analysis?
rationale: The request spans several runtime layers and asks for estimates or measurements, so automation cannot choose the measurement environment, accepted signal set, or whether the answer should be a docs runbook, code instrumentation, or both.

options.title: Runbook first
options.body: Document a native-Linux tracing procedure and quick-win config guidance using current telemetry, then open narrow issues for measured gaps.

options.title: Instrumentation first
options.body: Wait for or sponsor targeted telemetry PRs such as reply/context latency decomposition before writing the analysis.

options.title: Support-only close
options.body: Treat this as environment-specific support and close only if maintainers decide not to maintain performance runbooks for bespoke VPS configs.

recommendation.title: Runbook first
recommendation.body: Document a native-Linux tracing procedure and quick-win config guidance using current telemetry, then open narrow issues for measured gaps.

likelyOwner.reason: Current docs/runtime evidence and recent blame route through Peter Steinberger, making him the best available owner for scoping the runbook versus instrumentation path.
